Create an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican using html/3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.
Building your animated surfing pelican — non-interactive 3D scene on the way.

arguments.content: Surfing Pelican non-interactive · pure three.js animation

# Surfing Pelican

Animated, non-interactive 3D scene built with three.js.

- `index.html` — entry point, loads `main.js` as an ES module.
- `main.js` — whole scene: procedural low-poly pelican on a surfboard,
  animated ocean swell, curling wave with foam crest, wake, spray,
  drifting clouds, and circling gulls. No user input; camera is fixed
  and everything animates from the render clock.

Run locally with any static server, e.g. `npx serve .`, then open the page.

Built the animated, non-interactive surfing pelican page in the current directory.

What it is: a fixed-camera three.js scene of a low-poly pelican (grey body, orange beak and throat pouch, flapping wings, crest feathers) riding a red surfboard. It carves back and forth across a stylized curling wave with a foam crest, trailing wake, spray particles, an animated ocean swell, drifting clouds, and circling gulls. Everything is procedural in code with no assets, no user input, and no storage or network use.

Files: [index.html](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-spark-1.3-mc-low-20261017-090728/work/index.html) (entry point, loads `main.js`), [main.js](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-spark-1.3-mc-low-20261017-090728/work/main.js) (scene and animation loop), [README.md](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-spark-1.3-mc-low-20261017-090728/work/README.md), plus `three` installed via npm and imported by name.
